title: Annotatio I §.IV: Do not confuse proposition-propriety with real supernatural presence and manducation
pass_a_gloss: Yet to those Interpretations of the Reformers’ doctors of the Eucharistic proposition it is especially to be annotated: The question of the propriety or impropriety of Christ’s Eucharistic proposition is not here to be confused with the question either of the presence or of the manducation of Christ’s body in the Supper, real and substantial: nor from the denied Prior — i.e. from denied propriety of the words — is the negation of the posterior rightly inferred, i.e. negation of real presence and manducation. The prior negation regards words and terms, or the proposition composed of words and terms; the posterior the thing itself and its attributes. The prior, taken formally, is more Logical; the posterior more Metaphysical. Christ’s proposition This, i.e. this bread is my body, can be improper, even if Christ’s body, which is here improperly predicated of the bread, is properly — i.e. in truth — both present in the Eucharist and eaten, namely in a supernatural and spiritual mode imperceptible to us. For just as not by the asserted propriety of Christ’s proposition alone is His body asserted present in the Supper in a supernatural mode and eaten in the very thing, so neither by the denied propriety of the same proposition alone is His body denied present or eaten in the very thing in a supernatural mode. The supernatural and spiritual presence and manducation of Christ’s body — and those most highly real and substantial (designating that unique mode of presence and manducation of His body defined by Christ, both within and outside the Eucharist) — are understood more than enough from John 6 and 1 Cor. 10 and admitted without all controversy, even if the definitive Institution proposition This is my body is defended as improper or figurative and tropical after the manner of all definitive Sacramentals.
pass_b_english: Do not mix the propriety of Christ’s Eucharistic proposition with the question of real substantial presence and manducation in the Supper.
Deny propriety of the words, and you still have not denied real presence or eating — the first fight is logical (words/terms); the second metaphysical (the thing).

This bread is my body can be improper while Christ’s body is truly present and eaten supernaturally and spiritually (John 6; 1 Cor. 10) — just as asserting propriety alone does not prove that presence.
source_text: Ad quas tamen Reformatorum doctorum Interpretationes propositionis Eucharisticae, oppidò annotandum est: Non confundendam hic quaestionem de proprietate vel improprietate propositionis Christi Eucharisticae, cum quaestione, sive de praesentia, sive de manducatione corporis Christi, in Coena, reali ac substantiali: neque enim ex negata Priori, i. e. ex negata proprietate verborum, rectè infertur posterioris negatio i. e. negatio praesentiae & manducationis realis. Prior negatio verba spectat & terminos, seu propositionem ex verbis & terminis confiatam; posterior rem ipsam hujusque attributa. Prior, formaliter accepta, Logica magis, posterior verò magis Metaphysica. Propositio Christi: Hoc, i. e. hic panis est corpus meum, potest esse impropria, etiamsi corpus Christi, quod impropriè de pane hoc loco praedicatur, propriè, i. e. reverâ in Eucharistia & praesens sit & manducetur, supernaturali scilicet & spirituali nobisque imperceptibili modo. Sicuti enim, non per solam propositionis Christi assertam proprietatem, corpus ejus in Coena supernaturali modo praesens asseritur reque ipsâ manducari, ita nec per solam propositionis ejusdem negatam proprietatem, corpus ejus supernaturali modo vel praesens, vel re ipsâ manducari negatur. Praesentia pariter ac manducatio corporis Christi supernaturales & spirituales, eaeque quàm maximè reales & substantiales, (unicum illum à Christo definitum praesentiae & manducationis corporis sui, tàm intra, quàm extra Eucharistiam, modum designantes) ex cap. 6. Johan. & 1. Cor. 10. satis superque intelliguntur & citra omnem controversiam admittuntur, etiamsi propositio Institutionis S. Coenae definitiva: Hoc est corpus meum, ad modum definitivarum Sacramentalium omnium, impropria seu figurata ac tropica defendatur.
